Here is a 5-sentence summary of the article:

The paper proposes DiffTry (Differential Retries), a lightweight, stateless mechanism that assigns different retry-attempt limits to different priority classes of requests in microservice architectures, thereby transforming retries into a distributed rejection-prioritization tool that protects high-value transactions during overload periods without requiring overload detection or inter-service coordination. The authors develop an analytical model for DiffTry, first analyzing its behavior in a single overloaded service using fluid-model and queueing-theoretic approaches, then generalizing the framework to arbitrary networks of services by extending the standard open-network flow model to incorporate class-specific retry limits. They prove that the iterative solution method for computing per-class rejection rates in networks always converges, establish uniqueness guarantees for DAG-structured transaction flows, and demonstrate system-wide monotonicity showing that success rates for each class increase with retry limits. The model is validated through simulations and a live Kubernetes deployment where DiffTry is implemented as a simple drop-in service-mesh plugin, with measured rejection rates closely matching the analytical predictions. The results show that DiffTry substantially reduces the impact of both incidental and adversarial overload attacks—for example, high-priority transactions can account for roughly 85% of successful completions even when both classes contribute equally to input load—while also suppressing retry storms and unnecessary over-scaling costs.

summary_responses.response: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is issuing a direct final rule to make technical revisions to its Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) regulations, incorporating statutory amendments enacted in January 2021 and December 2023. The rule broadens FMLA eligibility by allowing virtually all Federal civilian service and certain honorable active military service to count toward the 12-month qualifying service requirement, while also clarifying that annual and sick leave provided under authorities outside of title 5 may be substituted for unpaid FMLA leave. Additionally, the rule excludes certain Veterans Health Administration (VHA) employees from title 5 FMLA coverage, as they are now governed by a separate FMLA provision under 38 U.S.C. 7425(c). Because FMLA eligibility is a prerequisite for paid parental leave (PPL), these changes also affect PPL eligibility for Federal employees. The rule is effective December 14, 2026, unless significant adverse comments are received by November 16, 2026, in which case OPM will withdraw the affected provisions and issue a notice of proposed rulemaking.
